flawed_step: 0019 | {{qed}} — the preceding steps establish only that g is an order-preserving ring monomorphism from Z into D; they do not establish that g is onto D, as required by the stated conclusion.
counterexample: Take D = Q with its usual addition, multiplication, and order. This is an ordered integral domain with characteristic 0. Here g(n)=n·1_Q=n, so im(g)=Z. But 1/2 ∈ Q and there is no integer n with g(n)=1/2. Thus g is not onto Q, directly refuting the stated conclusion.
assessment_summary: Steps 0001–0018 correctly establish characteristic zero and the canonical order-preserving embedding Z→D. The final QED is unjustified because surjectivity onto an arbitrary ordered integral domain is false; uniqueness is also not proved.
